tasks.question: Why does the test function that validates SQL rule fixes use a three-phase sequence of linting, fixing, and linting again instead of testing components independently?
tasks.reference_answer: generic_roundtrip_test invokes lint with selected rules and expects exit 1, invokes fix and expects 0, then lints the modified file with the same rules and expects 0 (test/rules/std_roundtrip_test.py:15-46). This integration test verifies detection, persisted correction and subsequent compliance for that fixture and rule selection. It does not independently prove a second fix leaves bytes unchanged or that unrelated rules are satisfied.

tasks.question: Why does the method that dispatches dialect warnings integrate with the CLI formatter's output routing mechanism to ensure warnings are properly formatted and routed?
tasks.reference_answer: dispatch_dialect_warning calls format_dialect_warning then _dispatch (src/sqlfluff/cli/formatters.py:216-218). The former creates and colorizes the warning (596-604); the latter sends nonempty text to the configured output stream (111-118). This shares formatting and destination handling. _filter_empty filters whitespace-only messages, not verbosity, and this dispatcher has no verbosity condition.

tasks.question: Why is the occurrence sorting method implemented as a static method within the Python format string templating class rather than as a standalone utility function?
tasks.reference_answer: _sorted_occurrence_tuples is a static helper that expands occurrence lists and sorts by position then text (src/sqlfluff/core/templaters/python.py:453-462). _slice_template calls it through cls (464-477), which groups it with templater operations and permits subclass replacement through that lookup. It needs no instance state. These are observable consequences, not documented reasons excluding a standalone helper; a helper in the same module would not require an import.
